stories.headline: Earthquake of magnitude 5.7 jolts Pakistan's Balochistan
stories.title: Earthquake of magnitude 5.7 jolts Pakistan's Balochistan
stories.summary: Islamabad, Oct 17: A 5.7-magnitude earthquake struck Pakistan's Balochistan province on Saturday, the US Geological Survey (USGS) said. The quake struck near Khuzdar town in Balochistan province, the USGS posted on X. The quake was reported 48 km west-northwest of Khuzdar, it said. In February, a 5.6-magnitude earthquake also struck Balochistan province. The earthquake struck at 6:30 am at a depth of 13 km, and its epicentre was 86 km northeast of Khuzdar town. The quake shook Jhal Magsi, Jaffarabad and Nasirabad in Balochistan, while tremors were also felt in several districts of neighbouring Sindh province, including Sukkur, Qambar, Shahdadkot, and Dadu districts. The deadliest earthquake hit the nation in 2005, killing more than 74,000 people. According to experts, Pakistan often experiences tremors as it lies on three major tectonic plates, including the Arabian, Eurasian, and Indian, which create five seismic zones under the country.

stories.headline: Flood Devastation to Festive Hope: Dibrugarh Pandal Honours Assam Survivors
stories.title: Flood Devastation to Festive Hope: Dibrugarh Pandal Honours Assam Survivors
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: In a striking departure from festive grandeur, the Masterpara Durga Puja Committee in Dibrugarh has unveiled its highly anticipated theme for this year's celebrations: “A Ray of Hope Amidst the Flood”.
The thoughtfully crafted pandal shifts focus directly onto the devastating environmental and humanitarian crisis that recently ravaged Upper Assam.
Built on a modest budget, the artistic installation vividly depicts inundated village landscapes, stranded families, and rescue boats.
It specifically highlights the intense hardships faced by communities in the worst-hit Sivasagar and Charaideo districts, where overflowing rivers breached traditional embankments earlier this year.
By positioning Goddess Durga at the centre of the waterlogged replica, the committee highlights a message of inner strength and solidarity.
The pandal also pays tribute to the tireless rescue operations led by the Indian Army and NDRF personnel.
This timely tribute coincides with major regional developments, including the resolution of a high-profile 14-day political protest in Guwahati.
Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma recently assured the release of critical rehabilitation and financial compensation packages for thousands of displaced families across Upper Assam.
Through this creative endeavour, Masterpara successfully transforms a cultural space into a profound reminder of human resilience.

article_sentences: Former Rajasthan Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot on Saturday (October 10, 2026) accused the BJP of trying to discredit the opposition for raising questions over the Election Commission.

He condemned BJP national president Nitin Nabin's remarks about dealing strictly with protesters and alleged that the BJP and RSS were portraying opposition protests as attempts to destabilise the country.

Mr. Gehlot alleged that instead of answering questions raised by the opposition over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, Mr. Nabin was acting as a lawyer of the Election Commission.
"Rattled by questions, BJP National President Shri Nitin Nabin is now having to act as the Election Commission's lawyer," Mr. Gehlot said in a post on X.
Speaking to reporters, Mr. Gehlot questioned mr.
Nabin's remarks about dealing strictly with those staging protests.
"Deal strictly with whom?
The people of this country?
Is it appropriate to use such language against people holding protests in a democracy?
Is it right to threaten them?" he asked.
Condemning the language used by the BJP president, Mr. Gehlot alleged he could not have made such remarks without instructions from Union Home Minister Amit Shah.

"When the president of the ruling party uses language as if he were a Minister or the Home Minister, it means he has received instructions from the government on what to say at the press conference," Mr. Gehlot alleged.

stories.headline: Indian national held in US over alleged illegal voting in 2024 presidential election
stories.title: Indian national held in US over alleged illegal voting in 2024 presidential election
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The charges carry a combined statutory maximum of 10 years in prison if the sentences are imposed consecutively, although any actual sentence would be determined by the court.

Washington: An Indian national has been arrested in the United States for allegedly misrepresenting his citizenship status to cast a vote in the 2024 general election in Minnesota, the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) announced on Friday.
The accused, identified as Chaudhari, faces federal charges of knowingly providing false information while voting and falsely claiming US citizenship to register or participate in an election.
According to the DHS, the charges stem from an incident on November 5, 2024, when Chaudhari allegedly signed a voter signature certificate required under Minnesota election law.
By signing the document, he affirmed that he was an American citizen, a requirement for participating in US federal elections.
However, federal prosecutors allege that Chaudhari was not a US citizen at the time and knowingly submitted the false declaration to cast his ballot.
The indictment includes two counts related to the alleged election violations.
“If convicted, he faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison on each count,” the DHS said.
Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the investigative arm of DHS, said it would continue pursuing cases involving alleged violations of federal election laws.
“Voting is reserved for US citizens, and falsely claiming citizenship to cast a ballot is a serious crime,” said Special Agent Travis Pickard of Homeland Security Investigations.
“HSI has the experience and authority to investigate these cases, and we take that responsibility seriously.
We will continue working with our law enforcement partners to protect the integrity of our election systems,” Pickard said.

opening: Trump’s Russia sanctions waiver eases one source of uncertainty for Indian markets as the Sensex and Nifty extend their recovery, led by IT stocks.
However, crude prices topping $110 a barrel remain a key risk.
body: Washington, Oct 17: US President Donald Trump has issued a waiver from sanctions, restrictions and duties under the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, citing national interest.
In an executive order on Friday night, Trump said that it is in the US "national interests" to withhold some of the sanctions.
"I am hereby waiving the application of such sanctions, restrictions, and duties provided for in the Graham Act," Trump said.
Trump said he had submitted to Congress a certification that issuing such a waiver at this time is in the national interest of the United States.

The Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act empowered Trump to impose sweeping sanctions on Moscow and slap steep tariffs against the world's largest purchasers of Russian oil and gas, including China and India.
The Graham Act, as it is now called, was passed by the US Congress on September 16 and signed into law by Trump two days later.
The law authorised Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent within 30 days of its enactment on all goods brought into the US from the five largest importers of Russian crude oil or gas.
The law also has a provision in Section 115 that allows the President to grant waiver from the application of sanctions, restrictions and duties if such a step is in the national interest of the US.
"Pursuant to section 115(a) of the Graham Act, I hereby waive the application of any duties provided for in sections 112 and 113 of the Graham Act or this order," Trump said.
Section 113 of the Graham Act deals with imposition of tariffs upto 100 per cent on countries that purchase Russian origin crude oil or natural gas or facilitate sanctions evasion.
The waiver from application of the act comes days after President Trump struck a deal with Russia for supply of diesel to the US and global markets.
It also comes days ahead of US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit to India.
External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar had raised concerns about the Graham Act during a meeting with Rubio on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York last month.
Jaishankar is understood to have conveyed to Rubio that oil refineries in India were configured largely for handling medium sour crude, which is supplied by Middle East countries and Russia.
He also told Rubio that Venezuela supplies heavier grade crude and the US has light grade crude which would require blending before being used by refineries in India.
With oil supplies from Middle East countries hit due to the Iran war, India has to depend on Russian crude to keep its economy running.

article_sentences: Kolkata: The father of the junior doctor who was raped and murdered at Kolkata’s state-run RG Kar Medical College and Hospital in August 2024 on Saturday threatened to launch a fresh movement in West Bengal following the Supreme Court’s decision to grant bail to former hospital principal Sandip Ghosh in a financial irregularities case.
A Supreme Court division bench comprising Justice MM Sundresh and Justice Prasanna B Varale on Friday granted bail to Ghosh, citing his prolonged incarceration and the slow pace of the trial.
“I will see it through to the end.
Even if necessary, I will call for a fresh movement in the state on this issue and hit the streets,” Sekhar Debnath, father of the junior doctor, told mediapersons.

Asked whether a fresh agitation would amount to a protest against the current BJP-led state government, particularly when his wife, Ratna Debnath, the victim’s mother, is a legislator of the ruling party, he said the political circumstances would not deter him from seeking justice for his daughter.
“It really does not matter that she is a part of the ruling dispensation.
I will do whatever is necessary for justice,” the victim’s father said.

Information about alleged large-scale financial irregularities at RG Kar, where Ghosh was the principal during the previous Trinamool Congress government led by Mamata Banerjee, surfaced after the junior doctor’s rape and murder in August 2024.
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested Ghosh in connection with alleged corruption at the state-run medical institution.
The victim’s parents had subsequently alleged that influential people were involved in their daughter’s death.
Debnath has now warned that he could return to the streets to protest against the latest development, renewing his demand for justice.
Ghosh had approached the Supreme Court after the Calcutta High Court rejected his bail plea.

stories.headline: India gets tariff reprieve as Trump waives Russian oil penalties, but the threat lingers
stories.title: India gets tariff reprieve as Trump waives Russian oil penalties, but the threat lingers
stories.summary: Delhi’s energy sourcing stays guided by national interest; experts warn threat of revived tariffs could be used as leverage in trade talks
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: US President Donald Trump’s decision to waive punitive tariffs on countries buying Russian oil and gas gives India relief from the threat of additional duties of up to 100 per cent on its exports to the US.
But it leaves Washington with the option of reviving the penalties, potentially using them as leverage in ongoing bilateral trade agreement (BTA) negotiations, experts noted.

New Delhi’s position on sourcing crude oil from Moscow and other countries will continue to be guided by its national interest and energy security, even as the order provides for continued US monitoring of Russian oil purchases and allows US President Donald Trump to withdraw the waiver and reimpose punitive tariffs, sources tracking the matter told businessline.

“Indian officials had been in discussions with their US counterparts over the implications of the legislation and the possibility of a waiver and there was optimism that it would happen after Trump struck a diesel deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin to supply the American and global markets with Russian refined fuel.
New Delhi’s stance on sourcing energy based on its national interest remains unchanged and interactions with Washington would continue,” the source said.
For India, the waiver buys time to negotiate a trade deal but offers no lasting certainty, pointed out Ajay Srivastava from trade research body GTRI.

Despite Russia’s share of Indian oil imports declining from 51 per cent in July to 44 per cent in August, as India bought more from the US and from the UAE, Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 (SRIA) remains law leaving Washington free to revive the tariff threat to extract concessions in bilateral trade talks.
“India should protect its energy security, buy oil on commercial terms and prepare for renewed US pressure.
Temporary tariff relief is no basis for permanent trade concessions,” Srivastava said.
In an executive order dated October 16, Trump waived the duties and several sanctions provisions under the Lindsey O. Graham SRIA, which he signed into law on September 18.

stories.headline: UNSC divisions stall process to elect next UN Secretary-General
stories.title: UNSC divisions stall process to elect next UN Secretary-General
stories.summary: United Nations, Oct 17 : The election for the next secretary-general is deadlocked, with the top three candidates getting two negative votes each from permanent members and only 76 days left for a new leader to succeed Antonio Guterres. In the straw poll held on Friday (local time), UNCTAD head Rebecca Grynspan, with nine overall positive votes, was slightly ahead of former Guyana Foreign Minister Carolyn Rodrigues-Birket and International Atomic Energy Agency Director-General Rafael Grossi, all of whom got two negative votes from permanent members. This was the sixth round of anonymous, informal voting in the Council to assess the sentiments towards the seven candidates, and the first to use colour-coded votes to tell permanent members apart. The results are supposed to be secret, but they were leaked to PassBlue and 1for8Billion, which cover the UN in-depth. With the top three candidates now known to be opposed by two permanent members each, serious negotiations could start among the veto-wielders, and between the candidates and permanent members. Yet another possibility is for new candidates to spring up. The candidate who wins ten votes without a veto from a permanent member will be recommended to the General Assembly, which routinely rubber stamps the Council recommendation, usually made unanimously in the final stage. In the straw polls, members vote "encourage", interpreted as positive, "discourage", a negative, and "no opinion" or neutral and in the previous five there were no distinctions between the votes of the permanent members and elected members without veto powers. Grynspan, who is from Costa Rica, received a total of five negatives and one neutral. She led in five of the six polls, except the second one in August, when Rodrigues-Birket led the field. This time Rodrigues-Birket received eight positives, six negatives and one neutral, the same as Grossi. But he got only two positives from permanent members, while she got three. Olara Otunnu, a former UN under-secretary-general and Uganda's foreign minister, former Senegal President Macky Sall, and Maria Fernanda Espinosa, a former president of the General Assembly and Ecuador's foreign minister, got three negatives each from permanent members, and Ivonne A-Baki, a former Ecuadorian ambassador to the US, got five negatives. The international sentiment is strong for electing a woman to head the 80-year-old UN that has had nine men as secretaries-general. Latin America and the Caribbean have staked a claim because it has been 35 years since anyone from the continent has held the office after Javier Perez de Cuellar ended his term in 1991. Two who have been rumoured as last-minute entrants to the race if the deadlock continues are Lana Nusseibeh, the United Arab Emirates minister of state for foreign affairs, and Feridun Hadi Sinirlioglu, the secretary-general of the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe, who is from Turkey. The US under President Donald Trump may hold the key to who gets the nod by tenaciously holding on to its veto. According to reports, the US does not think any of the seven meet its bar, and Trump is said to want someone who will carry out a drastic reform of the UN. Headed by the World Cup Soccer and the award of FIFA's inaugural Peace Prize, he was reported in July to have floated the name of the international football association's head, Gianni Infantino. But the candidature of the controversial Swiss national was not taken seriously. --IANS al/sd/

stories.headline: Trump waives sanctions, tariffs on purchase of Russian oil and gas
stories.title: Trump waives sanctions, tariffs on purchase of Russian oil and gas
stories.summary: Move comes ahead of Marco Rubio’s India visit, easing threat of 100 per cent duties on major buyers of Russian oil
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: - Donald Trump invokes national interest to waive key sanctions and tariff provisions under the Graham Act.
- The law allows tariffs of up to 100 per cent on goods from major buyers of Russian oil and gas.
- The decision comes ahead of US Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s India visit, with New Delhi concerned about the impact on its energy security.

US President Donald Trump has waived key sanctions and tariff provisions under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, citing national interest, temporarily easing the threat of steep duties on countries buying Russian oil and gas.
In an executive order issued on the night of Friday, 16 October, Trump said it was in the US national interest to withhold the application of certain sanctions, restrictions and duties under the law.
“I am hereby waiving the application of such sanctions, restrictions, and duties provided for in the Graham Act,” Trump said.
He said he had submitted a certification to Congress stating that granting the waiver at this time was in the national interest of the United States.

The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, signed into law by Trump on 18 September, authorises sweeping sanctions against Russia and tariffs of up to 100 per cent on goods from major buyers of Russian-origin crude oil and natural gas, including India and China.
Section 115 of the Act allows the President to waive sanctions, restrictions and duties if he certifies to Congress that doing so is in the national interest.
Trump invoked this provision to suspend the application of specified sanctions and tariff measures under the law.
The waivers will remain in force until the President or the relevant administration officials determine that further action is warranted.
The decision comes days after Trump struck a deal allowing Russian diesel supplies to reach the US and global markets, with the administration seeking to ease pressure on energy prices.

stories.headline: Supreme Court asks for medical report of Kerala’s tallest captive elephant, pulls up State government
stories.title: Supreme Court asks for medical report of Kerala’s tallest captive elephant, pulls up State government
stories.summary: The elephant, Uttoly Raman, has been at the centre of an ownership dispute; the Supreme Court had put the animal under the State government’s custody in June
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (October 9, 2026) pulled up the Keralam government for its failure to inform the court of the measures taken to protect Uttoly Raman, the State’s tallest captive elephant, after the tusker’s custody was handed over to the government in June.
The court directed the authorities to place the latest medical examination report of the elephant, which has been at the centre of a long-running ownership dispute, before it on October 12.

A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu asked why these details had not been disclosed in the State’s affidavit and why the court had been kept in the dark about the steps taken to ensure the animal’s welfare.
The State’s counsel informed the Bench that there had been a delay in taking custody of the elephant from its caretaker, Krishnankutty, due to the Assembly elections in Kerala.
Expressing serious reservations over the submission, Justice Datta remarked, “It is a wonderful argument to make.
So, the Supreme Court order is not to be complied with all these months because there were elections?”
The Bench also sought to know when the transfer of custody had eventually taken place and why the fact had not been mentioned in the State’s affidavit.
The court further directed the State to ensure that the former caretaker, who has been accused of “commercially exploiting” the elephant, is not allowed to touch the animal.
The court had earlier pulled up the caretaker over his treatment of the elephant.
“The only love and affection you have for the elephant is for the love of money.

You have commercially exploited the elephant,” the Bench had told Mr. Krishnankutty, who was found guilty of contempt in June for violating an undertaking that the animal would not be used for commercial or temple activities.
The Bench then turned to the elephant’s present condition, seeking details of the medical care provided to it since the June order.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Issues Notice On Plea Challenging Allahabad HC Order Banning Hookah Bars In Restaurants
stories.title: Supreme Court Issues Notice On Plea Challenging Allahabad HC Order Banning Hookah Bars In Restaurants
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court recently issued notice to the State of Uttar Pradesh in a plea challenging the Allahabad High Court's order, which held that hookah bars and hookah services can not be provided even in "Designated Smoking Areas".

Vide order dated September 29, a bench of Justice Shekhar B Saraf and Justice Abdhesh Kumar Chaudhary dismissed a batch of connected petitions concerning the operation of hookah bars and the provision of hookah services in restaurants.

It held that hookah service in a Designated Smoking Area is also prohibited under Rule 4(3) of the Prohibition of Smoking in Public Places Rules, 2008, as amended in 2017, read with the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act, 2003 (COTPA).
A bench comprising Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe issued notice on a special leave petition filed by M/S. Good Luck Food And Beverages challenging the High Court's judgment.
It has also issued notice on a prayer for interim relief.
The High Court stressed that the right of non-smokers to breathe clean air in a public place cannot be abridged by the commercial interests of an establishment claiming a right to trade.
The issue before the High Court was not whether smoking tobacco through a hookah, in isolation, was prohibited.
The question was whether restaurants and similar establishments could provide hookah as a service in a Designated Smoking Area.
The High Court observed that the general rule under COTPA is prohibition of smoking in public places, while the Designated Smoking Area is an exception to that general prohibition.

It further noted that while a Designated Smoking Area permits smoking, it does not permit a restaurant to provide hookah service, because the amended Rule 4(3) prohibits "any service" in a smoking area.

Ultimately, the bench held that "operation of hookah bars and rendering of hookah services by restaurants in the State of Uttar Pradesh" is a flagrant violation of Rule 4(3) and contrary to the scheme and object of COTPA.
The High Court heavily relied on the 2017 amendment to Rule 4(3).

stories.headline: Supreme Court Directs Union To Create National Database On Child Sexual Exploitation & Abuse Materials (CSEAM) For Removal Across Platforms
stories.title: Supreme Court Directs Union To Create National Database On Child Sexual Exploitation & Abuse Materials (CSEAM) For Removal Across Platforms
stories.summary: The Court also issued directions to the social media intermediaries regarding the detection and removal of CSEAM.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Court also issued directions to the social media intermediaries regarding the detection and removal of CSEAM.

The Supreme Court has called for stronger technological and regulatory measures to detect and remove child sexual exploitation and abuse material (CSEAM) from the internet, including the creation of a comprehensive national database to enable the identification and removal of such content across social media platforms.

A Bench of Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice KV Chandran issued a series of directions to strengthen the existing framework for detecting, reporting and removing CSEAM, expressing concern over the continued circulation of such material despite the Court's 2024 directions in Just Rights for Children Alliance & Anr.
S. Harish & Ors.

The Court observed that the existing mechanism largely relied on individual instances of harmful content being reported and subsequently removed, without adequate coordination between platforms to ensure that the same material was detected and removed across the internet.
It noted that when one platform detects and removes CSEAM, the same content does not automatically get flagged and removed from other platforms.
This fragmented approach, the Court said, delays the removal of such material and allows its continued circulation.

The Bench observed that the lack of effective initiatives by regulatory authorities and social media intermediaries had left it with no choice but to intervene to establish a workable framework for protecting children online.
The Court directed the Union Government to create a comprehensive national database containing hash identifiers and URLs of confirmed CSEAM.
The database may be established within the existing Sahyog Portal or as a standalone repository.
Hash identifiers are unique digital fingerprints generated from images or videos, enabling platforms to identify matching content even when it is uploaded by different users.
URL listing, meanwhile, identifies internet addresses where such material is hosted, allowing platforms to block access to known sources.

stories.headline: Telangana CM Revanth to review El Nino impact, drought conditions on October 12
stories.title: Telangana CM Revanth to review El Nino impact, drought conditions on October 12
stories.summary: The action plan prepared by Telangana Cabinet sub-committee on drought mitigation, along with relief measures likely to be examined
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy will hold a special meeting with Ministers on October 12 to review the impact of El Nino and the prevailing rainfall deficit in Telangana, with a focus on relief measures for farmers and steps to address emerging water and power requirements.

The meeting is expected to take stock of conditions in areas that have received insufficient rainfall, the difficulties faced by farmers and the immediate interventions required to mitigate the impact of the dry spell.
Agriculture, irrigation, drinking water supply and the rising demand for electricity will be among the key issues on the agenda.
The move comes after an extensive discussion on the rainfall deficit at the recent State Cabinet meeting.
Telangana has recorded 17% less rainfall than normal, with drought-like conditions prevailing in nearly 235 mandals, according to official estimates cited by the government.
The State government has already adopted a resolution in the Legislative Assembly urging the Centre to declare drought-affected mandals and extend adequate financial assistance.
It has also sought a special package of Rs.
20,000 crore to help the State tackle the impact of the deficient rainfall.

The meeting on Tuesday is likely to examine the action plan prepared by the Cabinet sub-committee on drought mitigation, along with relief measures that need to be taken up in rainfall-deficient areas.
Suggestions emerging from political parties, consultations with farmers’ organisations and inputs from experts in various sectors are also expected to figure in the discussions.

stories.headline: Slick diplomacy: Trump’s crude u-turn on Russia sanctions bails out India
stories.title: Slick diplomacy: Trump’s crude u-turn on Russia sanctions bails out India
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: For months, MAGA supremo Donald Trump and his minions threatened to “crush” India’s economy for New Delhi’s purchase of Russian oil.
The economics has now caught up with the rhetoric.

Faced with soaring fuel prices at home and a widely forecast rout in the mid-term elections, the US President has reversed course and put most of the Russia sanctions on ice, effectively leaving India off the hook for now.

The presidential U-turn, announced in an executive order issued on Friday evening (when governments typically drop bad/embarrassing news), invokes the president’s authority to waive provisions of the Graham Act passed last month “in the national interests of the United States.” Among them: 500% tariffs on Russian goods; 100% tariffs on the five largest buyers of Russian oil and gas (which would include India); and 100% tariffs on the top facilitators of Russian sanctions evasion.

The waiver follows Trump's surprise announcement of a deal with Vladimir Putin to buy Russian diesel fuel, even as his administration has turned on Ukraine to end a war that began with Russia's invasion.
The deadline to implement the sanctions was to expire on Sunday, one month from the day the bill was passed.
This does not mean sanctions threat has disappeared.
The executive order leaves the administration room to reverse course if Trump or designated officials later decide that further action is appropriate.
In theory, the president retains leverage; in practice though, a threat that is announced, legislated, signed and then shelved risks becoming less an instrument of coercion than a negotiating prop.

For India, which faced the prospect of tariffs as high as 100 per cent on goods entering the American market under the legislation, the reprieve is welcome -- and well may it send a bill to Washington for economic advice rendered.
New Delhi repeatedly insisted that its energy purchases are governed by market conditions, supply security and affordability -- the very argument now being made by Washington.
It also maintained steadfastly that its energy decisions cannot simply be dictated by the political preferences of Western capitals.

The economics has now caught up with the rhetoric.
body: Faced with soaring fuel prices at home and a widely forecast rout in the mid-term elections, the US President has reversed course and put most of the Russia sanctions on ice, effectively leaving India off the hook for now.

The presidential U-turn, announced in an executive order issued on Friday evening (when governments typically drop bad/embarrassing news), invokes the president’s authority to waive provisions of the Graham Act passed last month “in the national interests of the United States.” Among them: 500% tariffs on Russian goods; 100% tariffs on the five largest buyers of Russian oil and gas (which would include India); and 100% tariffs on the top facilitators of Russian sanctions evasion.

The waiver follows Trump's surprise announcement of a deal with Vladimir Putin to buy Russian diesel fuel, even as his administration has turned on Ukraine to end a war that began with Russia's invasion.
The deadline to implement the sanctions was to expire on Sunday, one month from the day the bill was passed.

stories.headline: India's Tariff Clock Is Now Running And WTO Can't Stop It
stories.title: India's Tariff Clock Is Now Running And WTO Can't Stop It
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: U.S President Donald Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 into law on September 18, 2026, after it cleared the House of Representatives 262-159 and the Senate 86-11.
Section 113 of the Act gives the President 30 days from signing a deadline falling around mid-October, to fix a tariff of up to 100% on the top five buyers of Russian oil or natural gas.
There is a narrow exemption: countries importing less than 15% of their natural gas from Russia, and taking "significant" steps to cut that share further, can escape the duty.
India and China remain the world's two largest buyers of Russian crude.
New Delhi has consistently framed these purchases as a matter of energy security, not as financing for Russia's war in Ukraine.
The Graham Act does not ask why India buys.
It only asks whether India buys, and how much.
That distinction is the real story here, and it is why this moment deserves more than routine trade-news coverage.
This is not simply another round of tariff friction between two trading partners.
It is a legal instrument specifically engineered to operate outside the normal channels of trade law and bilateral diplomacy alike.

The Graham sanctions-tariff regime exposes a structural blind spot in WTO law that has sat unaddressed since 2019: a member facing tariffs framed as "national security" measures has almost no enforceable recourse, because the WTO's own security exception was written to be self-judging, and the one body capable of testing that judgment the “ Appellate Body ” has been non-functional for seven years.
India is not losing this argument because its position lacks merit.

stories.summary: The finance ministry on Saturday said the legislative history of the IDBI (Repeal) Act, 2003, a Delhi High Court judgement and successive Union Budget speeches reflect the evolution of its policy towards the strategic disinvestment of IDBI Bank. The Cabinet earlier this week approved strategic disinvestment of IDBI Bank by selling 60.72 per cent stake to Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings for about Rs 53,000 crore (USD 5.5 billion). The deal is the largest foreign investment in India's financial sector so far and a major milestone in the country's banking privatisation drive. In a clarification on the legislative developments regarding reduction in government holding in IDBI Bank, the ministry said the Delhi High Court on December 17, 2018, held that the IDBI (Repeal) Act, 2003, contained no prohibition against reducing the government's stake in IDBI Bank Ltd.
